tests.title: Ephemeris vs JPL Horizons
tests.method: Apparent airless az/el of Sun and Earth from each site (terrain + 1 m) at 5 UTC instants: SPICE azlcpo (LT+S, DE440s, MOON_ME) vs Horizons API (DE441, coord@301), angular separation of direction vectors.
tests.metric: p95 and max angular separation (deg), n = 40
tests.evidence: Horizons responses cached in scientific/cache/horizons/ (not versioned); serial requests with identifying User-Agent.
tests.notes: Agreement holds for these 40 sampled instants only, limited by the 1e-6 deg precision printed by Horizons. It is not a general proof of equality for every site, time or body.

tests.title: Vertical datum and registration: PGDA 5 m vs PDS LDEM 80 m
tests.method: PGDA 5 m DEM block-averaged to 80 m cells and compared with LDEM_80S_80M bilinear samples at the same polar-stereographic X/Y; also +/-80 m shifts.
tests.metric: median difference (systematic offset), MAD, best shift
tests.target: |median| < 2 m at every site and best shift = (0,0)
tests.notes: Exploratory first run on 2026-11-14 preceded writing this target (median 0.2-0.3 m observed); stated for transparency.

tests.title: Horizon range convergence
tests.method: Horizon at 1 m computed with sight lines truncated at 300 km vs full DEM coverage.

tests.title: Reproduce Barker et al. (2021) illumination class
tests.method: Our points are centroids of PGDA RoIs defined as regions with average illumination > 70% at 1 m between 2024-01-01 and 2026-01-01. Same period, height and definition (mean visible fraction of the solar disk), hourly.
tests.notes: Differences expected from limb darkening (not modelled here) and from using the RoI centroid rather than every RoI pixel.

tests.title: Context: PGDA 18.6-year average illumination map
tests.method: Our 2-year hourly mean at 1 m vs PDS AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 at the same point.
tests.target: qualitative only (different period, resolution and DEM)
tests.notes: Not a pass/fail test. Two of the points were chosen as PGDA maxima, which biases this comparison.

tests.title: Sanity: height monotonicity and a permanently shadowed pixel
tests.method: Horizon at 5 m must not exceed horizon at 1 m; a pixel flagged permanently shadowed in PDS LPSR_85S_060M (Shackleton floor, 80 m DEM near field) must receive no direct sunlight hourly over 2024-2026.
tests.metric: booleans; max solar-disk fraction at PSR pixel
tests.notes: PSR test uses the 80 m DEM as near field (no 5 m PGDA tile covers this pixel).
